character: Mel: everyday Kiwi woman, late 30s, a first-time small developer with her partner (the 'we'). The same Mel as 'Which Dave?', so the NZ series sounds like one person. General NZ accent, never broad or a caricature, not Australian. Dry, under-played, amused at herself: the joke is her own auction FOMO, never bidders, agents or auction houses. She talks to a mate, not to camera; product moments sound like the same person, no announcer lift, no tagline cadence. AI voice, never presented as a real customer or testimonial.
casting_line: Night before the auction. Our budget? A vibe. Margin goes red. Ouch. Bid with a number, not a feeling. Q-S-me dot co dot en zed.
voice: Mel: whichever NZ female voice wins casting in projects/2026-10-02-qsme-voice-casting (shortlist ⭐ Jenna 7R9vnLAE0ZSpY0xWp0mv, ⭐ Ellie BujbDaM2eT58IpdbIc8J). Same voice as 'Which Dave?'.

lines.on_screen: Night before / the auction. (frame 1) · Our budget: (0.42) · A VIBE. (0.70, yellow marker) · sticky note '$1.1m-ish? (felt right in the car)' slaps on at 1.10
lines.text_v2: Night before the auction. Our budget? A vibe.
lines.text_v3: Night before the auction. Our budget? [sighs] A vibe.
lines.delivery: Mel, half-admitting it to a mate. 'Night before the auction' is plain and a little tired. Small lift on 'budget?' as if she's asking herself, then a beat, then 'A vibe.' flat and falling, owning it. Not a joke voice, no grin. Land 'vibe' just after the marker slams (0.70) and before the note slaps on. Out by 3.05, before the whip (3.2).

lines.on_screen: So we ran the numbers. (3.52 to 5.3) · the Rough feasibility card, 'Your numbers, our arithmetic.', green underline on 'Rough feasibility' (3.95)
lines.delivery: Brisk, practical, slightly sheepish: the grown-up move, finally. Even stress, falling on 'numbers'. Out by 5.15.

lines.on_screen: Sale price: $1.2m a home. (5.38 to 7.26) · zoom on 'Sale price per home', 1200000 typed 5.64 to 6.09
lines.delivery: Reading it off as she types. Quick and conversational, Kiwi 'one-point-two' (no 'million'), light lean on 'home'. Out by 7.15.

lines.on_screen: Land price: the vibe. $1.1m. (7.34 to 9.26) · zoom on 'Land price', 1100000 typed 7.38 to 7.83
lines.delivery: Dry callback to the hook. 'Land?' small rising question to herself, a tiny pause, then 'The vibe.' flat, as if that settles it. The number is on screen; don't voice it. Out by 8.92.

lines.on_screen: 24% margin. Sweet as. (9.34 to 10.78) · Profit $698,000 and Margin on cost 24.1% in green, green ring on 24.1%
lines.delivery: Pleased with herself, a touch too pleased: the set-up for the fall. 'Twenty-four' bright, 'Sweet as' relaxed and very Kiwi (both words even, falling). Out by 10.72.

lines.on_screen: Then the builder's real rate. (10.86 to 12.46) · zoom on 'Build cost per m² — edit to your builder's rate', 4000 selected 11.27, 4900 typed 11.46 to 11.76
lines.delivery: The mood drops a notch. Flat and slower, a little lean on 'real'. Like she already knows. Out by 12.37.

lines.on_screen: Margin goes red. (12.54 to 14.3) · Margin on cost 10.1% in red, red marker loop draws 12.6 to 13.0
lines.delivery: Deadpan report, no drama, each word a touch lower. Out by 13.6.
Under her breath, a small wince, not a cry. A real beat of silence before it (13.6 to 13.85). Reject any take that sounds performed or rises. Out by 14.4.

lines.on_screen: Most we can pay: $917k. (14.76 to 16.54) · the green box 'What you could pay for the land to keep a 20% margin: $917,000', value ringed in green, the app's grey disclaimer in full below it
lines.delivery: Calm, decided, the turn of the story. 'Nine-seventeen' (as Kiwis say $917k) said clearly, falling. Not sad about it: relieved to have a number. Out by 16.47 so the paper slide and marker squeak have the stage.

lines.on_screen: That's the paddle limit. (18.1 to 19.56, lands on the $917k stroke) · sticky note 'WALK-AWAY NUMBER $917k', the old '$1.1m-ish?' note crossed out
lines.delivery: Firm and simple, like writing it in pen. Light lean on 'limit'. Out by 19.45, before the whip (19.58).

lines.on_screen: Next morning. / Note's on the paddle. (19.9 to 22.3) · windscreen with morning sky, dashboard clock 9:40 AM SAT, indicator ticking until 21.8
lines.text_v2: Next morning. Note's on the paddle.
lines.text_v3: Next morning. Note's on the paddle.
lines.delivery: Quiet, a bit nervous but organised, said in the car with the engine off. Two short phrases, small gap between. Out by 22.05.

lines.on_screen: Paddle stays down. (23.56 to 24.5) · the paddle drops slowly back down, 23.42 to 24.02
